elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 14.5 opens "Upon expiration or any termination of this Agreement," with no condition tied to a particular termination route, no Program Transfer carve-out and no request precondition, so it applies after every covered exit.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 states "transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — 90 days only; no six-month (or up to six months) period is stated.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 contains no pricing basis for the assistance; no "then-current rates" language appears anywhere in the inserted or retained text.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5: SFJ "shall export and deliver to PB, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, all data, records and materials generated, collected or held by SFJ or its Affiliates relating to the Product or the Clinical Trials." The 30-day clock runs from expiration/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format requirement is specified in Section 14.5; "export and deliver" carries no commonly used, machine-readable format standard.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 is silent on deletion or certification. Retained Section 10.3 certifies destruction only of Confidential Information, only "at the Disclosing Party's direction," with retention exceptions, and is not sequenced after the 14.5 data return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 applies "Upon expiration or any termination of this Agreement," curing the double condition in Section 14.3 (Section 14.2 terminations only, and only absent a Program Transfer).

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 obliges SFJ to "provide PB with transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — an unconditional stated duration, unlike the redacted clinical-trial transfer period in 14.3.4(ii).

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 14.5 requires export and delivery within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination of "all data, records and materials generated, collected or held by SFJ or its Affiliates relating to the Product or the Clinical Trials," which is the category of PB data held by SFJ under this development program.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted Section 14.5 supplies an unconditional expiry-or-termination trigger, a stated 90-day assistance period, and a 30-day export deadline measured from the exit event.

Preferred level is not complete: four elements are absent from operative language — a six-month assistance period, a then-current-rates charging basis, a commonly used machine-readable return format, and written certification of deletion sequenced after return. Retained Section 10.3 does not supply certification for this purpose because it is limited to Confidential Information, is triggered only at the Disclosing Party's direction, permits retention copies, and is not tied to completion of the 14.5 return.

Minimal: one concise inserted paragraph in the termination article, no deletions or paraphrase of existing text, and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no procedures, no preferred-only mechanics such as rates, format or deletion certification). Reference to "materials" alongside data is within the scope needed to make the export operative and does not add a requirement outside the fallback checklist.

Preserves intent: Sections 10.3, 14.3 and 14.4.3.2 continue to operate; the export/delivery duty coexists with 10.3's return-or-destroy-at-direction mechanic and the 10.3 retention exceptions, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Drafting note (not a defect at the fallback level): Section 14.5 is not added to the survival enumeration in Section 14.4, so if the counterparty argues non-surviving provisions lapse at termination, consider adding "14.5" to the surviving-sections list — but only if the counterparty raises it, since adding it now would exceed the fallback checklist.

If negotiating upward to the preferred position, the specific repairs are: change "at least ninety (90) days" to "up to six (6) months at SFJ's then-current rates"; add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export obligation; and add a sentence requiring SFJ, after such return, to delete the data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
